altText: Navy cover slide. For parents, GCSE and A-level. Text: A Christmas break that’s actually a break. Helping them plan revision without it taking over the holiday.

Slide titled Plan it once, together. Plan: early in the break, sit down once and let them fit short revision sessions around family plans. Days off: agree some whole days off, Christmas Day included. Rest is part of the plan. Little and often: an hour or two on a revision day is easier to keep up than one big cram before term.
Slide titled Try saying. Two cards. Try “Which days do you want off?” instead of “How much revision have you done?” Try “Want a hand writing the plan?” instead of “You should be revising.”

Slide titled If mocks are in January. Build up: ask when the first mock is; the plan can build up gently towards it in the last week. Routine: keep meals and bedtimes roughly normal, even on the lazy days. Highlighted: if they’re worried, listen first. The plan can wait until tomorrow.

altText: Navy cover slide. Mocks, GCSE English. Text: 3 mistakes in English papers, and the fixes. For Language and Literature, whichever board you sit.

Slide titled The three. 1, retelling the story. Fix: for each point, give a quote, then say what the words do and why the writer chose them. 2, long quotes. Fix: pick a word or short phrase and zoom in on it. Short quotes are easier to analyse. 3, running out of time. Fix: check the marks for each question and share your time to match. The biggest questions need the most.

Slide titled Short quote, zoomed in. Lady Macbeth: “Out, damned spot! out, I say!” Word: “damned”, she feels cursed, not just dirty. Effect: the exclamation shows panic breaking through. Theme: guilt she can’t wash off. Note: Macbeth is one option text. Do the same with a short quote from yours.

Slide titled Before the mock. Practise: do one timed question from a past paper for your board, then mark it with the mark scheme. Texts: check your set texts with your teacher, and learn five short quotes for each. Highlighted: save five minutes at the end to check spelling and punctuation in your writing.

altText: Reel, Lock It In number 7, GCSE Geography · tectonic hazards. Question: what happens at each type of plate margin? A diagram shows three rows: constructive, where two plates move apart; destructive, where an orange plate moves towards a navy plate and sinks under it; conservative, where two plates slide past each other. Text: Constructive (also called divergent): magma rises into the gap. Volcanoes and small earthquakes. Destructive (also called convergent), oceanic: the denser oceanic plate sinks. Explosive volcanoes, strong earthquakes. Conservative: plates grind past. Earthquakes, but no volcanoes. Memory trick: build, break, slide. Constructive builds new crust. Destructive destroys it. Conservative conserves it. Ends on: Save this. Lock it in. Lock It In number 8 next week. Join early access, link in bio.

posts.planGate: Metricool Free plan: schedule only after Rej has confirmed the Starter upgrade in chat
altText: Navy cover slide. Mocks, GCSE Science. Text: 3 mistakes in Science papers, and the fixes. Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Combined Science.

Slide titled The three. 1, describing when it says explain. Fix: describe says what happens; explain says why; if it says explain, you need a because. 2, calculations with no working. Fix: write the equation, put the numbers in, then the answer with its unit. 3, graph answers with no numbers. Fix: quote values from the graph, like rises from 10 to 40.

Slide titled Describe or explain? Example: the rate of a reaction goes up as the temperature rises. Describe, what: as temperature rises, the rate increases. Explain, why: particles move faster, so they collide more often and with more energy. Note: same question, two different answers. Read the command word first.

Slide titled Before the mock. Equations: check which equations your board gives you and which you need to learn. Practicals: go over the practicals on your spec (required or core practicals): method, variables and results. Highlighted: underline the command word before you start writing.
Navy end slide with Em’s three-circle avatar and the Educate Me AI logo. Text: Save this for your Science mock. Something new from Educate Me AI in January. Join early access, link in bio.
